sections.title: A perennial hedgerow climber
sections.text: Bush vetch is a scrambling perennial, usually about 0.5–1 m high or spreading, with tendrils that catch on nearby vegetation. Its pinnate leaves have several pairs of leaflets; short stalks carry clusters of lilac-blue, pea-shaped flowers. Pods are roughly 2–4 cm long. The plate's tendrils, leaflets, clustered flowers and narrow pod are consistent with the species.

sections.title: Ecology and use
sections.text: Root nodules host nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and the plant is used in grassland forage mixtures. Its presence in the pea family does not by itself establish that its seeds are safe to eat; this species is not treated here as a human food.
